passage: I am Tenzin, and I want to tell you about last term, because I am still sorting it out. Binita and I were together nine months. Whenever I planned to see friends, she said, "If you go, I won't cope. I might do something to myself." The first time, I stayed home, shaking. By the third time I realised I was scared all the time, and that I could not be her only help. I did not laugh it off. I took what she said seriously. I told her older brother and the college counsellor together, so it was not just me carrying it. And I told Binita that I care about her, that she deserves proper support, but that I would not stop seeing my friends out of fear. She was furious and cried. It hurt. I am still worried about her.

qa.q: How long were Tenzin and Binita together?
What was Tenzin feeling when Binita said she might do something to herself?
qa.a: Tenzin was scared. The first time Tenzin stayed home shaking, and later realised the fear had become constant.

qa.q: What was a wise part of how Tenzin responded?
qa.a: Tenzin took her words seriously and told her older brother and the counsellor rather than carrying it alone, while refusing to be controlled through fear. 🤍

qa.q: How might Binita have felt when Tenzin told others and set the limit?
qa.a: She was furious and cried, perhaps feeling exposed or afraid of being left. She may also be in real distress that needs proper support.

grounding: A partner threatens self-harm to stop the protagonist seeing friends; he takes it seriously, involves adults and professionals, and refuses control through fear.

passage: Hemant's train to Pune for his internship left at 6 a.m., and his bag was already by the door when Arnab's message came at 11 p.m.: 'If you go, I don't know what I'll do to myself.' It was the third threat in a month; the first two had come when Hemant visited his cousins. Hemant's hands shook. He called Arnab at once and stayed on the line. 'I'm taking this seriously. I'm calling your sister Pallavi now so you're not alone tonight.' Pallavi lived two lanes away and went straight over. With Pallavi beside Arnab on speaker, the three of them called a helpline together. Just past one, Pallavi texted: 'Calmer now. I'm staying. Counsellor tomorrow.' Hemant lay awake, sad and scared, but at dawn he picked up his bag. Caring for Arnab didn't mean handing over his future.

qa.q: What time did Arnab's message arrive?
What was Hemant feeling while lying awake?
qa.a: Hemant felt sad and scared for Arnab and torn about leaving, yet still decided to take the train.

qa.q: Which steps made Hemant's response safe that same night?
qa.a: Hemant stayed on the line, got Pallavi to go over so Arnab was not alone, and joined a helpline call, so real help was involved before morning.

qa.q: How might Arnab see Hemant's trip to Pune?
qa.a: Arnab may feel real fear of being left and treat the trip as abandonment, using the threat to hold on, which is why the distress needed help rather than obedience.

grounding: Shows a partner threatening self-harm to stop a trip, and the wise response of treating the distress seriously, involving family and a helpline that night, and not being controlled through fear.

passage: 'If you go to Rukmini's sangeet, don't bother calling me after,' Sahil said at the gate of Ritu's building in Lajpat Nagar. 'I'll know you never cared.' Ritu had heard versions of this before: when she joined the dance society, when she stayed late at the library. Each time she gave in, and each time the next demand came faster. That evening she sat on the kitchen floor while her mother chopped onions, and told her everything: the gate, the sangeet, the months before. Her mother put the knife down. 'That's not love talking. That's fear being used on you.' Together they found a counselling line for young adults, and Ritu booked a call for the next afternoon. Then she ironed her yellow kurta for the sangeet and set her phone face down.

qa.q: Where was Sahil standing when he made the threat?
qa.a: Sahil was at the gate of Ritu's building in Lajpat Nagar.

qa.q: What might Ritu be worried about as she sits on the kitchen floor?
qa.a: Ritu is afraid and worn down, worried that going to the sangeet will end things with Sahil and that giving in will only bring more demands.

qa.q: What helped Ritu stop being pushed around by the threat?
qa.a: Telling her mother everything, booking a counselling call, and then choosing to go to the sangeet anyway.

qa.q: How does Sahil want Ritu to see her trip to the sangeet?
qa.a: Sahil frames an ordinary outing as proof that Ritu doesn't care, turning it into a loyalty test that keeps control with him.

grounding: Shows a partner threatening to leave unless Ritu complies, and the wise step of bringing in a trusted adult and a counselling line instead of giving in to fear.
